# Life Recorder

> Life Recorder is a free Android app that keeps a rolling one-hour audio buffer
> on the phone; one tap saves the last minutes after the moment happened. Audio
> never leaves the device.

Life Recorder is a retroactive voice recorder for Android. Instead of starting
to record when you press a button, it listens continuously into a self-erasing
buffer of the last 60 minutes. When something worth keeping happens — a child's
first word, a great idea, an important sentence in a meeting — the user taps
save (in the app, on a home-screen widget, or on the notification) and the last
5, 10 or up to 60 minutes become a normal audio recording, even though the
moment already passed. Everything not saved is continuously and permanently
discarded.

Key facts:

- Platform: Android. Install: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.record.liferecorder
- Price: free; all features are currently unlocked (no account required).
- Privacy: the buffer, saved recordings and transcripts are stored only on the
  device, in the app's private storage (sandboxed from other apps, protected at
  rest by the phone's built-in encryption). Nothing is uploaded to the developer; there are no servers that
  receive audio. Audio leaves the phone only if the user shares a recording or
  enables backup to their own Google Drive.
- Transcription: on-device, about 100 spoken languages, automatically detected.
  A one-time speech model download (~380 MB) happens over Wi-Fi; after that it
  works offline.
- Editing: play with a waveform, trim to exact seconds, rename, share.
- Battery: built to sip power; optional recording schedule (listen only during
  chosen hours) and skip-silence (quiet stretches are not stored).
- Languages: the app UI is available in 30 languages, with right-to-left support.
- Legal note: recording laws differ by country; in some places all parties must
  consent. Users are responsible for complying with local law.
